scope: Single-slot F32 ROCm developer checks on one R9700; all required ROCm models with explicit per-row reference backend. Not final candidate/full hardware-matrix qualification.
method: The merged #36 baseline and numerical controls preserve their executable/archive identities and failures.

One predicate selects short MoE slot batching and the CLI-compatible warp scan. Request-local decode permission prevents cached scratch from changing later serial-prefilled requests. Numerical GPU kernel source and the release policy are unchanged.
Seven CPU policy tests cover prompt boundaries, mode transitions, MTP, opt-outs and unchanged backend/KV/concurrency cases. Both old policies fail their corresponding new tests.

Live reference generation uses the policy-pinned commit, batch 512, micro-batch 1, one slot, F32 KV and flash attention disabled. Qwen uses the worker canonical HIP build; Gemma uses the same pinned Vulkan build as earlier controls. Each backend and executable hash is recorded per model.

Each packaged model row checks its exact GGUF hash, 12 tokenizer corpus cases, all 48 CLI choices and three full HTTP reference cases in each of three phases: initial, after cancellation and after long-context/error recovery.
The initial MoE-fix package passed the MoE row but failed the new post-context checks for dense 27B and 9B. That unsuccessful sweep remains separate.

Actual OpenCode 1.19.4 runs directly against each identified package at 16K, with bounded tools, a fresh server per fixture and independent frozen tests. No synthetic responses, supervisor edits or tool repairs.
All GPU/model work is remote. Owned process groups and clients are stopped before their command returns.

negative_controls: Old short-slot routing fails the MoE batching-boundary regression.
Old scratch-only eligibility fails the short–long–short reuse regression.

remaining_limits: Unsigned previews and one-board developer checks do not qualify final release bytes or the other required Metal/Vulkan hardware profiles.
The model matrix uses explicitly identified HIP and Vulkan reference builds at the same policy commit; worker provisioning/final candidate qualification remain separate.
The new routing is scoped to default F32 single-slot B1 serving. Other KV/concurrency configurations retain their existing behavior and gain no new qualification claim.
The 16K MoE OpenCode trial is separate from required 4K model rows and from Gemma 31B OpenCode memory limits. Three core fixtures do not establish complete large-repository delivery.
No model catalog promotion, NVIDIA hardware validation or local workstation GPU/model inference was performed.
